set_from: CI scale run 40888941398, all four legs (the Intel Mac ran 3 to 4 times Linux on every timed metric, so its scale is 3.25; its code budgets keep 2.5, where the work-list refill read 1218 of 1250 ms). HARDEN-07, DEC-184.
_how: A budget is for 50,000 tracks (1,000 files for a tag write). A smaller run is held to it; a larger one is recorded, not held.

Base: the Windows number in docs/user-guide/performance.md times 1.5, or the Phase 15/16 budget where one exists; then the first CI scale run (set_from): a metric within 10% of its budget on any leg was raised to about 1.25 times its worst value, and one with room to spare was left alone.
A time under 10 ms is floored at 10 ms: below that a shared runner measures noise.
Where nothing was recorded (or the guide's number is out of date) the base is a first estimate from a Linux container run, said so in _basis.

A leg's scale multiplies every time budget (the Intel Mac's runner is 2.5 times slower than Linux; Windows is 1.5, for its disk: fsync and Defender); its overrides replace single budgets after the scale. Windows overrides a metric where 1.5 would be far looser than its measured value (about 1.25 to 1.3 times that value) or too tight (a migration is 5 to 17 times slower there: about 1.5 times). A leg's code_scale is the factor for budgets written in a bench's own code (scaled_ms); Windows has 1.0.
A leg that is more than twice as slow as the others is investigated, never loosened.

Ratio budgets (the waveform-analysis and decoder responsiveness limits, 1.5 times idle) are in those benches and are the same on every leg: a ratio compares a leg with itself, so no scale applies. The decoder's idle is floored at 100 ms, so a near-zero idle cannot make a ratio of noise (see recorded_only).

recorded_only.match_storage: bench_match_storage.py measures what storing match attempts costs (rows and megabytes per candidate); it is a size estimate, not a speed, so it is recorded in the run's JSON and has no budget
recorded_only.decoder: bench_decoder.py holds its own budget: the search p95 with four analyses running may be at most 1.5 times the idle p95 floored at 100 ms (RESPONSIVENESS_BUDGET, RESPONSIVENESS_FLOOR_MS), so 150 ms whenever idle is under 100 ms and the plain 1.5 ratio above it. The old plain ratio failed on every leg of the first CI run (2.02, 3.58, 2.58) because idle was about 10 ms on Linux: a ten-millisecond rise doubles a ratio over a near-zero base. Chosen over an absolute added time because it still scales with a slow idle. Nothing is scaled
recorded_only.waveform_analysis: bench_waveform_analysis.py holds its own ratio budget (RESPONSIVENESS_BUDGET); nothing is scaled. macOS arm64 read 1.57 in-engine in the first CI run (1.29 in a worker), perhaps contaminated by two 30 s decoder stalls on that run (DEC-229); it is left at 1.5 and watched

library._basis: Windows 11 desktop, performance.md, times 1.5; facet_small_ms: estimate (the guide's 7 and 12 ms predate the facet queries; 33 and 57 ms on Linux, times 1.5); statistics_* are the Phase 15/16 budgets; first CI run 40888941398: import_s 20.5 and refresh_apply_s 25.5 (macOS arm64 read 16.10 and 20.09 against 16.4 and 21, about 1.27 times); statistics_health_ms 620 (Linux read 491 against 500, about 1.26 times; above the Phase 15 target of 500 ms, see above_spec); Windows runs these at scale 1.5 (reimport, refresh_apply, browse_sort and import then sit 27 to 30% over what Windows measured), and its health at 800

clean._basis: Windows 11 desktop, performance.md, times 1.5; first CI run: Windows file_check_s 17 and health_report_ms 525 (1.3 and 1.27 times its 13.12 s and 411 ms); the other legs keep these, with room

migrations._basis: m0025: the Phase 16 budget (1 s; 324 ms recorded). m0027: estimate, 58 ms on Linux, floored at 1 s; first CI run: Windows keeps m0025 at 1.0 (0.813 s there) instead of scaling it

search_keys._basis: m0033: about 0.6 s recorded at HARDEN-06 and 1.07 s on Linux, times 1.5; the rest: estimates from a Linux run (m0032 0.28 s, search 1.3 ms, count 30 ms); first CI run: Windows m0032 6.8 s (4.498 s measured, 17 times Linux's) and m0033 5.3 s (3.537 s), 1.5 times the measured value so a real regression still shows

engine_start._basis: estimates from a Linux run on 308 MB (first /health 0.69 s from source, launch copy 2.1 s, library ok 2.1 s, one migration pending 3.6 s, quick_check 0.74 s), about 4 times that; the packaged one-file engine on a Mac takes about 10 s to unpack on a cold start, so the Macs have their own first_health_ms; first CI run: Windows launch_backup_s 10.5 (8.063 s), pending_state_ok_s 18.5 (14.588 s, 15 was a near miss) and pending_migrate_s 10.3 (6.833 s, 8 times Linux's)

tag_write._basis: estimate: 1,000 files through the checked copy took 2.95 s on Linux; Windows is slower (fsync, antivirus)

e2e._basis: estimates (nothing was measured in the packaged app but the renderer: 186-222 MB, times 1.5): the import is the engine's 10.9 s times 1.5 plus the job's own overhead; first CI run: import_s is now the import job alone (the strip check, reload and Library navigation are outside the timed window); the set value is the measured 19.18 / 45.28 / 27.17 s less the 5 s strip wait, times 1.25 (Windows 51 s), so check it against the next run; renderer_mb 410 (macOS arm64 read 329 against 350)

above_spec.note: Phase 15's target is under 500 ms. Linux read 491 ms (9 ms from it), macOS arm64 428 and Windows 640, so Windows already misses the target. Budgeted at 620 (Windows 800) so the check does not flake; HARDEN-10 should look at the Health query.

above_spec.metric: work list refill and count (WORK_LIST_BUDGET_MS in bench_waveforms.py)
above_spec.note: Phase 11's work-list budget is 500 ms at p95. The refill read 469 / 428 / 476 ms (Linux / Windows / macOS arm64), within 6% of it on every leg. Budgeted at 600; HARDEN-10 should look at the work-list query.
